heard: The WOW signal lasted 72 seconds, the telescope's exact view limit. On August 15, 1977, Ohio State University's Big Ear Telescope picked up the powerful anomaly. Astronomer Jerry R. Amann discovered the signal while reviewing computer printout data. Amann circled the intensity reading 6EQJ5 and wrote WOW beside it. The signal frequency hit around 1420 MHz, matching the neutral hydrogen emission line. In 2024, scientists found a magnetar flare hitting a gas cloud could cause it. Despite decades of searches, the mysterious anomaly from the constellation Sagittarius has never recurred. This natural fluke is what created the 72-second signal, lasting the exact duration the telescope could watch.
